Ten E.coli cells with 15N - dsDNA are incubated in medium containing 14N nucleotide. After 60
minutes, how many E.coli cells will have DNA totally free from 15N?
(1)
20 cells
(2)
40 cells
(3)
60 cells
(4)
80 cells
Molecular Basis of Inheritance
subject: Biology
b6_reason: E. coli divides every 20 min, so 60 min gives three generations (80 cells); the 20 original 15N strands end up in 20 hybrid cells, leaving 60 cells with DNA entirely of 14N.
b6_working: Generations = 60/20 = 3. Total cells = 10 x 2^3 = 80. Each starting cell has 2 heavy strands, which are conserved semi-conservatively into 2 hybrid daughter cells, so hybrid cells = 10 x 2 = 20. Cells free of 15N = 80 - 20 = 60.
b6_note: Requires the standard assumption of a 20-minute E. coli generation time, which the stem does not state.
